words.en: Completely free means without any cost or charge, entirely without payment.

words.tr: phrase. 无付款；未支付；无需付款
words.ex: There is no payment for this service.
words.ex_cn: 这项服务不需要付款。
words.en: The absence of payment for goods or services.

words.tr: v. 卖；销售；“sell”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He sold his old bike last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周卖了他的旧自行车。
words.en: If you sell something, you give it to someone in exchange for money.

words.ex: This book is not expensive.
words.ex_cn: 这本书不贵。
words.en: Not expensive means costing little money; affordable or inexpensive.

words.tr: phrase. 性价比高的；物有所值的
words.ex: This phone is good value for money.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机物有所值。
words.en: If something is good value for money, it is worth the amount of money that you pay for it.

words.tr:
n. 费用；代价；
v. 花费；
words.ex: The cost of the book is ten dollars.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的费用是十美元。
words.en: The amount of money that you need in order to buy, make, or do something.

words.tr: v. 买得起；担负得起；有时间做；
words.ex: I can't afford a new car.
words.ex_cn: 我买不起一辆新车。
words.en: If you cannot afford something, you do not have enough money to pay for it.

words.ex: He is a wealthy man who owns many houses.
words.ex_cn: 他是个富有的人，拥有许多房子。
words.en: A wealthy person, organization, or country has a lot of money, resources, or assets.

words.tr: phrase. 商业的业务；商业活动；指以盈利为目的的企业或贸易行为
words.ex: He runs a small commercial business selling books.
words.ex_cn: 他经营一家小型商业企业，出售书籍。
words.en: An organization or activity that buys and sells goods or services for money.

words.tr: phrase. 对…额外收费；为…加收费用
words.ex: The hotel will make an extra charge for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 酒店会为早餐额外收费。
words.en: To require an additional payment for something beyond the standard fee.

words.ex: There is an additional fee for late registration.
words.ex_cn: n. 逾期注册需要支付额外费用。
words.en: An extra charge that is added to the original cost.

words.tr: phrase. 全部费用已付的旅行；由他人或机构承担所有费用的旅程
words.ex: He won an all-expenses-paid trip to Paris.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得了一次全包的巴黎之旅。
words.en: A trip where all costs are covered by someone else, such as an employer or a contest sponsor.

words.ex: He used vouchers to buy food.
words.ex_cn: 他用代金券买了食物。
words.en: A voucher is a piece of paper that can be used instead of money to pay for something, or that allows you to pay less than the usual price of something.

words.tr: phr. 提供激励措施和财务福利
words.ex: The company is offering incentives and financial benefits to keep workers happy.
words.ex_cn: 公司正在提供激励措施和经济福利以留住员工。
words.en: Providing rewards, advantages, or benefits to encourage a particular behavior or action.

words.tr: 它花费如此之多（指价格昂贵）
words.ex: It costs so much to buy a new phone.
words.ex_cn: 买一部新手机要花这么多钱。
words.en: It is very expensive.

words.ex: We all know that cost of too high is not acceptable.
words.ex_cn: 我们都知道成本太高是不可接受的。

words.tr: 短语. 赚钱能力已经提高了
words.ex: His earning power has gone up after he got a new job.
words.ex_cn: 他找到新工作后，收入能力提高了。
words.en: The capacity to earn money has increased.

words.tr: phrase. 更高的可支配收入（指个人或家庭在扣除税收和其他必要支出后可用于消费或储蓄的收入）
words.ex: With higher disposable income, people can afford to travel more.
words.ex_cn: 随着更高的可支配收入，人们可以负担更多的旅行。
words.en: Higher disposable income refers to the amount of money that households have available for spending and saving after income taxes have been accounted for.

words.ex: His income is enough to pay for rent and food.
words.ex_cn: 他的收入足以支付房租和食物。
words.en: Income is the money that a person or a company earns regularly, for example from investment or work.

words.ex: This phone is affordable for students.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机对学生来说价格合理。
words.en: If something is affordable, most people have enough money to buy it.

words.ex: The price is reasonable for a good quality phone.
words.ex_cn: 这部质量不错的手机价格合理。

words.w: devote a large portion of their budgets
words.tr: phrase. 将他们预算的很大一部分用于
words.ex: Many companies devote a large portion of their budgets to research and development.
words.ex_cn: 许多公司将预算的很大一部分用于研发。

words.ex: He invested a lot in his new business.
words.ex_cn: 他在这项新业务上投资了很多。

words.tr: adj. 更便宜的；“cheap”的比较级；
words.ex: This shirt is cheaper than that one.
words.ex_cn: 这件衬衫比那件更便宜。
words.en: Comparative form of cheap: costing less money than something else or than is usual.

words.ex: Many products go down in price during sales.
words.ex_cn: 许多产品在促销期间降价。

words.ex: My parents give me a weekly allowance.
words.ex_cn: 我父母每周给我零用钱。
words.en: An allowance is money that is given regularly, usually to a child, by their parents, or by the government to someone who is unemployed or ill.

words.ex: I need the money for the bill.
words.ex_cn: 我需要这笔钱来付账单。
words.en: Money is the coins or bank notes that you use to buy things, or the amount of these that you have.

words.ex: This meal is not a complimentary service; you have to pay.
words.ex_cn: 这顿饭不是免费服务，你必须付钱。

words.tr:
n. 收费；负责；指控；
v. 收费；充电；
words.ex: The hotel charge is $50 per night.
words.ex_cn: 酒店的收费是每晚50美元。
words.en: If you charge someone, you ask them to pay an amount of money for something that you have sold to them or done for them.

words.tr: phrase. 没有额外收费；免费；不另收费
words.ex: There is no extra charge for delivery.
words.ex_cn: 送货没有额外费用。
words.en: If there is no extra charge for something, you do not have to pay more money for it in addition to what you are already paying.

words.tr:
adj. 免费的；自由的；
adv. 免费地；自由地；
v. 释放；
words.ex: The museum offers free entry on Sundays.
words.ex_cn: 这个博物馆在周日免费入场。
words.en: If someone is free, they are able to do what they want to do, or go where they want to go, without being controlled or restricted.
